companyDescription: Affordable jet-drone + C-UAS + space domain awareness + hypersonics · Valkyrie CCA (USMC program of record) · ~$692M in fresh DoW contract/funding wins since early July · Q2 earnings TODAY (Aug 4, after close)
priceNote: Up 5.60% on Aug 3 close to $49.21, rebounding off the 52-week low ($43.09) ahead of tonight's Q2 print (after market close, Aug 4). Refreshing this pick — three fresh DoW contract/funding wins since mid-July have strengthened the thesis further, even as the stock remains ~63% below its Jan 2026 high of $134.
summary: Since the last update, Kratos landed two more major DoW awards on top of the Jul 13 space domain contract: ~$400M in accelerating hypersonic/national-security program funding (Jul 14) and a ~$156M counter-drone (C-UAS) IDIQ from the DoE's Office of Secure Transportation (Jul 21) — roughly $692M in combined contract/funding news since early July, each driving a same-day +3% to +9% pop. Q2 2026 earnings land TODAY after the close (Zacks consensus EPS $0.13, revenue $411.7M, +17.1% YoY), but Kratos has a real, documented pattern of the stock falling even on beats — Q1 2026 beat by 23%+ and the stock still fell 7.34% that day. Named-firm targets now range widely (Clear Street $84, Wedbush $85, Goldman Sachs $89, Stifel $134, Noble Financial $145), averaging well above the current price. The contract/funding cadence — not tonight's print — remains the more reliable near-term driver.

catalysts.name: Q2 2026 Earnings — TODAY
catalysts.description: Reports after market close Aug 4, 2026 (call at 5pm ET). Zacks consensus EPS $0.13 (+18.2% YoY), revenue $411.7M (+17.1% YoY). Kratos beat on earnings in each of the trailing four quarters (avg surprise 22-26%) — but has an unusual, documented pattern of the stock falling anyway (Q1 2026: beat 23%+, stock fell 7.34%). Nearest dated event, but historically a lower-conviction catalyst than contract/funding news.

catalysts.name: $400M DoW Hypersonic + National-Security Funding
catalysts.description: Announced Jul 14, 2026 — funding pace from the Department of War accelerated from June into July; CEO cited the Nemesis/Kraken hypersonic initiatives and positioned Kratos as the only company delivering both propulsion and flyer systems for hypersonics. Stock popped +3.6% to +4.9% same day. More hypersonic-related awards expected in coming months.

catalysts.name: $156M Counter-Drone (C-UAS) DoE Contract
catalysts.description: Sole-source IDIQ awarded Jul 21, 2026 by the DoE's National Nuclear Security Administration (Office of Secure Transportation, Project Solar Shield) for mobile Counter-Unmanned Aircraft System platforms. Stock gained +3% to +4.3% same day — the third funded award of the month following the $100M space domain contract (Jul 13) and $36M air defense award (Jul 2).

risks: Kratos has an unusual, real pattern of NEGATIVE earnings-day reactions even on beats — Q1 2026 EPS beat estimates by 23%+ and the stock still fell 7.34% (max intraday -8.5%) that day; tonight's Aug 4 print carries the same demonstrated risk despite a strong beat streak (avg surprise 22-26% over the last four quarters)

Valuation remains stretched even after the pullback — P/E near 275x, stock still down ~19% YTD and ~63% below the Jan 2026 high of $134 — leaving room for further multiple compression if growth decelerates or DoW funding pace slows

Feb 2026 public offering (14.29M shares at $84, ~$1.17B raised for capex + Nomad/Orbit M&A) added roughly 7-8% to share count — strengthens the balance sheet for scaling but is a permanent EPS-dilution overhang investors may still be re-pricing

Fed held at 3.50-3.75% in July but with 3 hawkish dissents wanting a hike, and inflation still above target — next FOMC Sept 15-16; a hawkish surprise could pressure high-multiple growth/defense names broadly even though DoW appropriations themselves are policy-, not rate-, driven
Contract/funding cadence, while strong (~$692M across three awards since Jul 2), remains lumpy and unscheduled — a pause in DoW award flow would remove the stock's most reliable near-term driver

estimateDates.note: Reports today after market close — historically a lower-conviction catalyst than contract/funding news for this specific stock given its negative-leaning earnings-day pattern
The real near-term driver — 3 awards totaling ~$692M landed since Jul 2 alone; CEO flagged more hypersonic-related awards expected in coming months

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed held at 3.50-3.75% at the July 2026 meeting, but 3 FOMC members dissented wanting a hike, and inflation remains above the 2% goal. Next decision is Sept 15-16. DoW/DoE program spending itself is policy-driven and largely rate-insensitive, but the broader hawkish tilt raises risk for high-multiple growth names generally.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Inflation is 'elevated relative to the Committee's 2 percent goal' per the July statement, with resurgent energy-price pressure prompting some forecasters to expect higher, not lower, rates before year-end.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: MEDIUM. Defense names are typically more insulated from a hawkish-Fed tape than high-multiple tech since procurement is set through appropriations, not monetary policy — but KTOS's own elevated valuation (P/E ~275x) leaves it exposed to multiple-compression risk in a genuine risk-off move.
macroRisk.summary: Fed risk stepped up to MEDIUM from the prior LOW read — the July FOMC held rates but with a notably more hawkish dissent (3 members) than before, and inflation is still running hot. The contract/DoW-funding thesis is largely policy-driven and decoupled from the rate cycle, but tonight's Aug 4 earnings print adds its own idiosyncratic risk (documented negative reactions even on beats) on top of a slightly less benign macro backdrop than three weeks ago.
